messages.author: 14297cca791bf77f
messages.subject: BIC model evaluations
parts: Is there a way to get likelihood value from the fitqtl output in order to test different models with BIC?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] BIC model evaluations
parts:
The output of fitqtl() is a list that includes a component named "lod" which is the LOD score relative to the null model. So the log10 likelihood, up to a constant. So that should be what you need.

data(hyper)
hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper, step=1, error.prob=0.002)
qtl <- makeqtl(hyper, chr=c(1,4), pos=c(48.3, 29.5), what="prob")
out.fq <- fitqtl(hyper, qtl=qtl, method="hk")
names(out.fq)
# [1] "result.full" "result.drop" "lod"
out.fq$lod
# 12.87841

karl

parts:
Thank you. I just want to verify I use it correctly:
The LOD is already the logarithm so when I use it in the formula, I do not perform the log() again.
as in:  BIC=<- (-2)*out.fq$lod + 2*log(n)*df  ; df being the number of QTL in the model, and n the number of individuals
I use log(), equivalent of lnfunction,  not log10()

is that correct?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] BIC model evaluations
parts:
LOD is on the log 10 scale, so you'd want to multiply by log(10) to get it onto natural log scale.

(-2)*out.fq$lod*log(10) + 2*log(n)*df

karl
